query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the spray distance during HVAF-i7 deposition to approximately 300–350 mm will enhance the in‐flight particle velocity, thereby increasing the deposition efficiency sufficiently to overcome the thickness limitation while maintaining coating integrity and low oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: Gas-atomized FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder (15–45 μm feedstock) that has previously shown optimal quality with the HVAF-M3 system.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 torch setup to use a longer spray distance (300–350 mm), which is known from conventional MCrAlY bond coat studies to yield higher particle velocity and improved deposition efficiency.
generation.conditions: Deposition performed on substrates (including those with internal diameters as small as 120 mm) under elevated-temperature thermal barrier service conditions, maintaining low as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.structural_mediator: The increased travel distance provides particles with higher kinetic energy, leading to better melting, flattening upon impact, and adhesion. This results in a more homogeneous and thicker build-up of the coating with controlled oxidation levels.
generation.mechanism: A longer spray distance boosts particle velocity and momentum; upon impact these higher-energy, adequately melted particles form a thicker, well-adherent deposit. The improved kinetics help balance the trade-off between deposition rate and in-flight oxidation by reducing the time particles are exposed to oxygen, thus preserving the desired phase composition.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline condition using a shorter spray distance, the thicker coating will be deposited without sacrificing the mechanical integrity or increasing oxidation. This improved deposition should yield a bond coat that meets both the thickness and high-temperature durability targets.
generation.baseline: HVAF-M3 coatings using 15–45 μm powder produce high-quality, adherent layers, whereas the HVAF-i7 with the same feedstock at its standard (shorter) spray distance yields acceptable quality but with inadequate thickness.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective for HVAF-i7 systems under conditions similar to the conventional MCrAlY spraying studies. Its efficacy may be limited if the torch design or substrate geometry (e.g., extreme curvatures well beyond 120 mm) significantly alters particle dynamics.
generation.uncertainty: While the mechanism is supported by conventional spray studies, the quantitative increase in coating thickness and the exact trade-offs between increased particle velocity and potential microstructural changes remain to be precisely determined via experimental trials.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform parallel HVAF-i7 deposition trials on identical substrates using the standard spray distance (baseline) and the adjusted longer spray distance (300–350 mm). Ensure all other parameters (feedstock size, powder feed rate, substrate pre-treatment, etc.) remain constant. Post-deposition, measure coating thickness, microstructure, adhesion, and oxidation levels.
measurements: Microstructural phase analysis via XRD and SEM
Oxidation level assessment via EDS mapping
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coating deposited at 300–350 mm does not show a significant increase in thickness compared to the baseline, or if it exhibits compromised adhesion or increased oxidation that degrades performance under high-temperature service, then the hypothesis is falsified.
